purpose: Planning-stage registry for poker rules, education research, reusable data candidates, correctness references, and product-safety boundaries.

records.title: 2024 Poker TDA Rules, Recommended Procedures, and Illustration Addendum
supports: Terminology and edge cases used in organized tournament poker
A review checklist for misdeals, all-ins, action order, and procedural fairness
does_not_support: A universal cash-game rules specification
Heads-up strategy recommendations
Permission to reproduce the rulebook verbatim
records.notes: Tournament-specific. Project rules remain a versioned local specification backed by tests.

records.title: 2026 WSOP Tournament Rules and Live Action Rules
records.scope: WSOP 2026 event and live-action house rules linked from the official event page.
supports: A current example of a major operator's tournament and live-action rules
Terminology and operational edge-case comparison
does_not_support: A universal No-Limit Hold'em cash-game standard
Permission to republish WSOP documents
Any strategy baseline
records.notes: Use only as a named house-rules reference and keep it distinct from the app's heads-up engine contract.

records.title: Poker Hand Dataset
supports: Independent five-card hand-category test vectors
Educational examples about hand classes and class imbalance
does_not_support: Seven-card Hold'em evaluator correctness by itself
Betting rules, ranges, equity, EV, or strategy
Real-world player behavior
records.notes: Download and hash the exact files before use; preserve attribution required by CC BY 4.0.

records.title: Poker Hand History File Format Specification
records.publisher: University of Toronto Computer Poker Research Group
records.scope: Human-readable, machine-friendly hand-history format covering multiple poker variants.
supports: A future interchange format for manual hand-history import and export
A vocabulary for durable, replayable hand records
does_not_support: Automatic permission to ingest histories from poker operators
A strategy or solver baseline
Replacement of the TypeScript engine's state-transition rules
records.notes: MIT covers the specification. Operator-specific imported histories still require separate policy and privacy review.

records.title: Poker Hand Histories Dataset
records.publisher: University of Toronto Computer Poker Research Group
records.scope: Collection in PHH format spanning multiple sources and 11 poker variants; repository points to a larger Zenodo release.
supports: Testing PHH parser coverage against varied hand shapes
Researching historical hand-history interoperability
does_not_support: Assuming every collected hand has the same commercial reuse rights as repository code
Treating observed player actions as correct strategy
Training user-specific opponent models
product_uses: Potential parser fixtures after record-level review
records.notes: The repository is MIT, but it aggregates hands from different upstream sources. Rights and privacy must be checked per layer before any ingestion.

records.title: PokerKit
records.publisher: University of Toronto Computer Poker Research Group
records.scope: Python library for multi-variant poker simulation, hand evaluation, and statistical analysis.
supports: Independent differential tests for selected rules and hand-evaluation fixtures
Research into multi-variant state and hand-history modeling
does_not_support: Replacing the pure TypeScript runtime engine without a separate architecture decision
A GTO strategy baseline
Correctness of Holdem Lab merely because both implementations agree
records.notes: Pin an exact release and keep any Python tooling outside the browser runtime. Agreement is evidence, not proof.

records.title: OpenSpiel
records.scope: Research framework for games and learning algorithms; includes poker environments such as Kuhn, Leduc, and Hold'em via ACPC/PokerKit integrations.
supports: Reference experiments for imperfect-information games
Small-game CFR and legal-action oracle comparisons
does_not_support: Drop-in browser production architecture
A ready-made 100BB heads-up strategy dataset
Any claim that Hold'em is fully solved
records.notes: Useful for R&D and small-game verification; not evidence for production solver accuracy.

records.title: pokersolver
records.scope: JavaScript evaluator for up to seven cards with winner and tie comparison.
supports: A lightweight differential reference for hand-category and winner fixtures
Browser/Node interoperability comparison
does_not_support: Betting rules or pot settlement
Equity or strategy conclusions
Replacing existing tested evaluator behavior without parity review
records.version: repository master; pin commit before use
records.notes: Its broader game variants are outside v1 scope. Prefer curated fixtures over adding a runtime dependency.

records.title: poker_solver
records.scope: Open-source heads-up no-limit solver project with Python reference and Rust core.
supports: A candidate local R&D path for reproducible solver experiments
Examples of differential testing and explicit solver limitations
does_not_support: Publishing its output as Holdem Lab solver data without independent convergence and configuration review
Production-scale flop accuracy based only on repository claims
A multiway strategy baseline
records.notes: The project itself documents unvalidated production-scale flop/turn limits. Any result must retain seed, tree, ranges, iterations, exploitability metric, hardware, and exact version.

records.title: postflop-solver
records.scope: Rust postflop solver for Texas Hold'em.
supports: High-level feasibility research
Identification of relevant public algorithms and solver UX patterns
does_not_support: Copying code into an intended non-AGPL product
Treating generated solutions as licensed training content
A preflop or multiway product baseline
records.notes: AGPL is a material product-license decision. Do not port implementation details into the planned application.

records.title: DeepStack: Expert-level artificial intelligence in heads-up no-limit poker
records.scope: 2017 Science paper; DOI 10.1126/science.aam6960; heads-up no-limit research system evaluated over 44,000 hands.
supports: Poker as a serious imperfect-information AI research domain
The technical difficulty of heads-up no-limit strategy computation
does_not_support: A reusable strategy dataset
A claim that an unrelated heuristic is GTO
Multi-player conclusions
records.notes: Cite the research; do not imply that its system or data powers Holdem Lab.

records.title: Superhuman AI for multiplayer poker
records.scope: 2019 Science paper about six-player no-limit Hold'em; DOI 10.1126/science.aay2400.
supports: The importance and difficulty of multi-player imperfect-information strategy
Why six-player expansion is a separate research and engineering scope
does_not_support: A downloadable complete six-max strategy
Transferring heads-up guarantees to multiplayer play
Calling heuristic feedback solver data
records.notes: Useful for explaining why multiplayer strategy cannot be inferred from a heads-up engine.

records.title: Poker as a Domain of Expertise
records.publisher: Journal of Expertise / University of Helsinki
records.scope: 2020 review of poker expertise, decision-making, learning, and emotion self-regulation.
supports: Framing poker as structured decision-making under uncertainty
Including learning and self-regulation in the curriculum
does_not_support: Specific hand or betting recommendations
Claims that training guarantees financial performance
A complete curriculum efficacy result
records.notes: CC BY permits attributed reuse, but product adaptations should still be independently authored and reviewed.

records.title: Retrieval Practice Consistently Benefits Student Learning: A Systematic Review of Applied Research in Schools and Classrooms
records.scope: 2021 systematic review of 50 classroom experiments and 5,374 learners.
supports: Using active recall instead of passive reading as a default learning loop
Testing knowledge repeatedly with feedback
does_not_support: A claim that Holdem Lab has already improved learning
One universal quiz format for every concept
Generalization without product-specific experiments
records.notes: The review notes that only 6% of included experiments were conducted in non-WEIRD countries.

records.title: A systematic review of interleaving as a concept learning strategy
records.scope: 2021 systematic review focused on interleaving during concept learning.
supports: Mixing confusable board textures or decision types when contrast aids concept discrimination
Using interleaving selectively rather than as a decorative randomizer
does_not_support: Interleaving every long or complex exercise
Random scenario generation without learning objectives
A poker-specific effect size
records.notes: Apply first to short, easily confused examples and measure transfer before expanding.

records.title: The Distributed Practice Effect on Classroom Learning: A Meta-Analytic Review of Applied Research
records.scope: Applied review of distributed versus massed practice in classroom learning.
supports: Spacing reviews across sessions instead of encouraging one long cram session
A due-review queue after initial learning
does_not_support: A specific scheduling algorithm for poker decisions
Daily streak pressure as an educational requirement
Guaranteed retention
records.notes: Confirm article-level license before adapting any figures or text.

records.title: Impact of performance and information feedback on medical interns' confidence-accuracy calibration
records.scope: Randomized study of accuracy feedback, explanatory information, and confidence calibration in a medical-learning context.
supports: Recording confidence alongside correctness
Testing whether explanatory feedback improves calibration
does_not_support: Assuming a confidence slider automatically improves judgment
Transferring medical-task results to poker without validation
Using confidence as a skill score by itself
records.notes: Treat confidence as a metacognitive signal and report sample size; do not reward high confidence alone.

records.title: Responsible Gambling Resources
records.scope: Consumer-protection and gambling-harm education resources in the United States.
supports: Clear signposting to independent help resources
A product policy that learning content should not glamorize gambling or hide risk
does_not_support: A legal compliance opinion for every country
Marketing an education app as harm-free
Copying helpline content without checking location and freshness
records.notes: Support links must be localized and rechecked before launch. Holdem Lab remains an education product, not a gambling operator.

records.title: Third Party Tools and Services Policy
records.scope: First-party policy distinguishing study aids from prohibited real-time assistance and data mining.
supports: A strict no-real-time-assistance product boundary
Avoiding client detection, current-table reading, automated actions, and opponent data mining
does_not_support: Approval of Holdem Lab by PokerStars
Permission to use the product while any specific poker client is running
A universal policy across operators
records.notes: Operator policies can change. The safest product rule is stronger: no table connection, no screen/card detection, and no advice tied to a live hand.
